summary.text: Assuming the claimed additive identity, the shifted tail \(c_m=a_{3773+m}+1\) satisfies the Fibonacci recurrence; modulo \(p=195318521017\), a finite computation of \(c_0,c_1\) together with fast-doubling Fibonacci arithmetic at \(j=249580073232\) gives \(c_{j+1}=c_{j+2}=1\), so \(p\) divides two consecutive terms. Their gcd is therefore at least \(p>1\), but for positive consecutive terms the defining value \(g+(u+v)/g\) with \(g\ge2\) cannot equal \(1+u+v\), contradicting the assumed identity.

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)_{n\geq 1}\) be the sequence defined by
\[
a_1=a_2=1,
\qquad
a_n=\gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2})+
       \frac{a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}}{\gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2})}
       \quad(n\geq 3).
\]
We disprove the assertion that all three displayed formulas in the conjecture hold for every \(n\geq3775\). In fact, it is enough to disprove the first one,
\[
 a_n=1+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}. \tag{1}
\]
Since the conjecture asserts a conjunction including (1), failure of the universal assertion (1) already disproves the full conjecture.

We will argue by contradiction. Assume that
\[
a_{3775+m}=1+a_{3774+m}+a_{3773+m} \tag{2}
\]
for every integer \(m\geq0\).

First note that every \(a_n\) is positive. This is immediate for \(a_1,a_2\). If two successive terms are positive, then their gcd is positive, and the formula defining the next term expresses it as that positive gcd plus a nonnegative integer. Thus positivity follows by induction.

We use the modulus
\[
p=195318521017
\]
and the integer
\[
N=249580073232.
\]
No primality property of \(p\) is needed; only \(p\geq2\) matters in the final step.

Define, with values in the residue ring \(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\),
\[
c_m=a_{3773+m}+1. \tag{3}
\]
The assumed identity (2) gives a homogeneous Fibonacci recurrence for \(c_m\). Indeed,
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_{m+2}
 &=a_{3775+m}+1\\
 &=\bigl(1+a_{3774+m}+a_{3773+m}\bigr)+1\\
 &=\bigl(a_{3774+m}+1\bigr)+\bigl(a_{3773+m}+1\bigr)\\
 &=c_{m+1}+c_m.
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
This equality actually holds over the integers under our assumption, and hence also modulo \(p\).

Let \(F_0=0,F_1=1\), and \(F_{r+2}=F_{r+1}+F_r\). The standard closed form for any sequence satisfying (4) is
\[
c_{m+1}=F_{m+1}c_1+F_m c_0 \pmod p. \tag{5}
\]
For completeness, this follows directly by induction on \(m\). At \(m=0\), the right side is \(F_1c_1+F_0c_0=c_1\). If the formula holds at two consecutive indices, adding those two identities and using the Fibonacci recurrence gives the identity at the next index.

We now record the two finite computations used in the argument.

First, direct iteration of the defining gcd recurrence through index \(3774\) gives
\[
 a_{3773}+1\equiv77940394259\pmod p,
 \qquad
 a_{3774}+1\equiv99768150822\pmod p. \tag{6}
\]
This is a finite integer computation, carried out as follows. Start with the ordered pair \((x,y)=(1,1)\). At each step put
\[
g=\gcd(x,y),\qquad (x,y)\longleftarrow
\left(y,\;g+\frac{x+y}{g}\right).
\]
After \(k\) steps, the pair is \((a_{k+1},a_{k+2})\), as follows immediately by induction from the definition of the sequence. Performing \(3772\) such exact-integer steps gives \((a_{3773},a_{3774})\); reducing the two entries after adding \(1\) gives precisely the residues in (6). The gcds in this computation are taken before reducing modulo \(p\), as required by the original recurrence.

Second, a Fibonacci doubling computation gives
\[
F_N\equiv117378126758\pmod p,
\qquad
F_{N+1}\equiv21827756563\pmod p. \tag{7}
\]
Here is a reproducible modular calculation of these two residues. If a current pair is
\((A,B)=(F_k,F_{k+1})\) modulo \(p\), use the identities
\[
F_{2k}=F_k(2F_{k+1}-F_k),
\qquad
F_{2k+1}=F_k^2+F_{k+1}^2. \tag{8}
\]
Thus, writing
\[
C=A(2B-A),\qquad D=A^2+B^2\pmod p,
\]
the next pair is \((C,D)\) when the next binary digit is \(0\), and \((D,C+D)\) when it is \(1\). Starting from \((F_0,F_1)=(0,1)\) and reading
\[
N=(11101000011100001000011011000100010000)_2
\]
from left to right produces the following trace. Each row lists the binary prefix already read and the resulting pair \((F_k,F_{k+1})\) modulo \(p\):
\[

This proves (7) using only the identities (8) and modular arithmetic. The first identity in (8), for example, follows from the Fibonacci addition formulas; the second is the familiar identity \(F_{2k+1}=F_k^2+F_{k+1}^2\).

It also follows from the Fibonacci recurrence that
\[
F_{N+2}\equiv117378126758+21827756563
          =139205883321\pmod p. \tag{9}
\]

Now apply (5) first with \(m=N\). Using (6) and (7), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_{N+1}
&\equiv F_{N+1}c_1+F_Nc_0\\
&\equiv
21827756563\cdot99768150822
+117378126758\cdot77940394259\pmod p.
\end{aligned}
\]
The integer on the last line is
\[
11326212385784681827108
 =57988419771\,p+1.
\]
Consequently,
\[
c_{N+1}\equiv1\pmod p. \tag{10}
\]

Likewise, (5) with \(m=N+1\), together with (6), (7), and (9), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_{N+2}
&\equiv F_{N+2}c_1+F_{N+1}c_0\\
&\equiv
139205883321\cdot99768150822
+21827756563\cdot77940394259\pmod p.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here
\[
15589577514788957011679
 =79816176334\,p+1,
\]
so
\[
c_{N+2}\equiv1\pmod p. \tag{11}
\]

Recalling the definition (3), congruences (10) and (11) say
\[
p\mid a_{3773+N+1},
\qquad
p\mid a_{3773+N+2}. \tag{12}
\]
Thus the two consecutive positive terms
\[
v=a_{3773+N+1},
\qquad
u=a_{3774+N+1}=a_{3773+N+2}
\]
are both divisible by \(p\). In numerical index notation, these are \(a_{249580077006}\) and \(a_{249580077007}\).

Let
\[
g=\gcd(u,v).
\]
Since \(p\) divides both \(u\) and \(v\), it divides \(g\). The terms are positive, so \(g>0\); because \(p\geq2\), it follows that
\[
g\geq p\geq2. \tag{13}
\]
Also, \(g\mid u\) and \(g\mid v\). As \(u,v>0\), each is at least \(g\), and hence
\[
u+v=gq
\]
for an integer \(q\geq2\).

The actual defining recurrence says that the term following \(u,v\) is
\[
g+\frac{u+v}{g}=g+q. \tag{14}
\]
On the other hand, the conjectured formula (2), used with \(m=N+1\), says that the same term is
\[
1+u+v=1+gq. \tag{15}
\]
But (13) and \(q\geq2\) make these two numbers unequal. Indeed,
\[
(1+gq)-(g+q)=(g-1)(q-1)>0. \tag{16}
\]
Thus the true recurrence (14) and the assumed formula (15) give contradictory values for the same term, namely \(a_{3775+(N+1)}=a_{249580077008}\).

The contradiction arose solely from assuming that the first conjectured identity holds for every \(n\geq3775\). Therefore that universal identity is false. Since it is one of the three simultaneously asserted identities in the OEIS conjecture, the full conjecture is false as well.
